overview: A one-page Department of State list of papers indexing correspondence filed under 894.91 concerning the Japanese press from 1930 to 1934. The listed papers cover a detailed historical and reference report on Japanese newspapers, the press’s affiliations and political complexion, the change in ownership and management of the Japan Times and Mail, a proposed government-supported merger of the Rengo and Nippon Dempo news services for propaganda purposes, and increasing Japanese government interference with the press. The sheet also points researchers to a related document filed under 894.00 P.R./82.

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers on the Japanese Press
subfiles.about: An index summarizes papers filed under 894.91 concerning Japanese newspapers, news agencies, propaganda, and government interference with the press between 1930 and 1934.
subfiles.summary: The sheet lists a 1930 Embassy report offering a historical survey and reference appendix on the principal Japanese newspapers, together with a Department commendation of that report. It also indexes Joseph C. Grew’s reporting on the affiliations and political complexion of the press and on Hitoshi Ashida’s takeover of the Japan Times and Mail. Later entries concern a rumored merger of Rengo and Nippon Dempo into a powerful government-supported propaganda service and the Japanese government’s increasing interference with the press, the latter cross-referenced to file 894.00 P.R./82.

interest: The sheet is useful as a compact roadmap to State Department reporting on Japan’s press during the early 1930s, linking newspaper ownership, political alignment, news-agency consolidation, propaganda, and state interference. It identifies a potentially valuable lost or separately filed reference report containing detailed descriptions of the principal newspapers. The chronological entries also suggest the progression from descriptive press analysis in 1930 to growing concern about centralized propaganda and government control by 1934.
